title: Symphony No. 104 in D major, “London”
hook: Haydn’s last symphony, written for London, opens in darkness and ends with a dance over a bagpipe drone.

painting.title: Westminster Bridge, with the Lord Mayor’s Procession on the Thames
painting.collection: Yale Center for British Art, New Haven
painting.pairingNote: London’s river on Lord Mayor’s Day, crowded with ceremonial barges; the rich, music-loving city that, half a century later, paid Haydn handsomely for his last symphony.

facts: Haydn spent two long spells in London, in 1791–92 and 1794–95, invited by the violinist and impresario Johann Peter Salomon. He wrote twelve symphonies for London audiences, and No. 104, composed there in 1795, is the last of them. It is also the last symphony he wrote.

It was played at a concert of Haydn’s own music, which he directed, at the King’s Theatre on 4 May 1795 (some sources date its first performance a few weeks earlier, in the same theatre). Haydn noted in his diary that the audience was delighted and that he had earned 4,000 gulden in one evening, adding: “such a thing is possible only in England.”
The nickname “London” is a little arbitrary, since all twelve were written for London. In Germany it is often called the “Salomon” symphony.
It is scored for pairs of flutes, oboes, clarinets, bassoons, horns and trumpets, with timpani and strings.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a solemn call out of the dark and a bright, single-minded Allegro (I), a gentle song with a storm in the middle (II), a sturdy dance (III), a folk-like finale over a drone (IV).

movements.heading: Adagio – Allegro
movements.summary: The symphony begins with a loud call on two bare notes, then quiet, anxious music in D minor. After about two minutes the clouds lift and the violins start a quiet, cheerful tune in D major. Haydn builds the whole fast section from that one tune: where a second theme would normally appear, he brings back the first in a new key. It is a [[sonata-form|sonata form]] with almost a single theme.

mainIdeas.name: The call
mainIdeas.description: the whole orchestra on two notes, D and A, with no third note to say whether the music is major or minor.

mainIdeas.name: The Allegro tune
mainIdeas.description: a light, smiling melody in the violins, first heard quietly.

stops.hear: The whole orchestra plays a loud, bare call and holds it; then the strings answer very quietly, in a sombre minor
stops.happening: The slow introduction, in D minor

stops.hear: The violins, quietly, start a bright tune in D major
stops.happening: The Allegro begins with its main theme

stops.hear: The full orchestra joins in, loud, with trumpets and drums
The same tune again, now in a new key, with the woodwinds
stops.happening: Where a second theme would be, Haydn reuses the first, in A major

stops.hear: The music turns quiet and restless; a rhythm from the end of the tune is passed around in minor keys
The tune returns in the violins in D major

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: Loud, confident closing bars

notice: In the opening seconds, notice that you cannot tell whether the music is happy or sad. The two notes leave it open, until the quiet strings choose the minor.
Count how often the Allegro tune comes back. Nearly everything in the movement grows from it.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Jochum recorded all twelve London symphonies with the London Philharmonic for Deutsche Grammophon in the early 1970s; No. 104 was made in October 1971. He does not repeat the exposition in the first movement, which is why it lasts about nine minutes. On the Spotify album, a set of all twelve, the symphony is tracks 21–24.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: A gentle, songlike theme in G major for the strings, the kind of tune you might hum. It is repeated with changes, then interrupted by a loud outburst that wanders through distant keys. When the theme returns, the woodwinds, especially the flute, add new colour.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: a simple, graceful melody in the strings, in short balanced phrases.

mainIdeas.name: The outburst
mainIdeas.description: the same melody turned loud and dark in the minor.

stops.hear: The strings, softly, play a simple, singing tune
stops.happening: The main theme, in G major

stops.hear: The tune darkens for a moment, then comes back with a bassoon doubling the melody
stops.happening: A short minor-key episode, then the theme varied

stops.hear: A sudden loud outburst for the whole orchestra; the harmony wanders
stops.happening: The middle section, through G minor and B-flat major

stops.hear: The music comes to rest on a held chord, as if waiting; then the theme returns
stops.happening: The return of the opening section

stops.hear: The flute decorates the melody high above the strings
stops.happening: The theme reworked, with the woodwinds to the fore

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The music grows quieter and closes gently

notice: Compare the theme at the start with its last appearance. The tune is the same; the instruments around it have changed.

movements.heading: Menuetto: Allegro
movements.summary: A [[minuet|minuet]], but a sturdy, outdoor-sounding one with strong accents. The middle section, the [[trio|trio]], moves to a distant key, B-flat major, and gives the tune to the oboe and bassoon.

mainIdeas.name: The minuet
mainIdeas.description: a strong, stamping tune in three for the full orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: a lighter, gentler tune for oboe and bassoon over soft strings.

stops.hear: A bold, stamping dance in three for the full orchestra
Softer and smoother; oboe and bassoon lead
A quiet link, then the stamping dance again

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A firm, loud close

notice: Listen for the change of colour when the trio begins. The key slips down to B-flat, far from home, and the woodwinds take over.

movements.heading: Finale: Spiritoso
movements.summary: The finale opens with a sound from the countryside: a low note held underneath, like the [[drone|drone]] of a bagpipe, and a lively, folk-like tune above. The tune is often said to come from a Croatian folk song, a claim that is disputed. Haydn sets it in a [[sonata-form|sonata form]] and, before bringing it back, lets the music linger in a strange, distant key.

mainIdeas.name: The tune
mainIdeas.description: a bouncy melody in the violins, over a long-held bass note.

mainIdeas.name: The drone
mainIdeas.description: a single low note sustained under the tune, as a bagpipe or hurdy-gurdy would.

stops.hear: A low held note, and above it the violins play a lively folk-like tune
The full orchestra bursts in
The music becomes restless; pieces of the tune are thrown between the instruments
Everything goes quiet and seems to lose its way, in a dark minor key
stops.happening: The development is extended, in F-sharp minor

stops.hear: The folk tune comes back over its drone

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: A last surge of energy, and loud closing chords

notice: Listen to the very first bars for the drone under the tune. It is the sound of village music, brought into a London concert hall.

threads.title: From darkness to light
threads.body: The symphony opens with a stark call in D minor and ends in a bright, rustic D major. The journey is made in the first two minutes and again across the whole work.

threads.title: One idea at a time
threads.body: In the first movement a single tune does the work of two; in the finale one folk melody carries everything. Haydn shows how much can come from very little.

threads.title: A farewell
threads.body: This is Haydn’s last symphony, written at the height of his fame, for an audience that had paid generously to hear it.
